screener.reading_rule: This screener opens on the newest 15-min reading that has contracts over the liquidity floors, which is not always the newest reading the store holds: a reading rebuilt from 15-minute candles carries no traded-price average, so no contract in it has a premium and none of them can clear the premium floor. Every reading the store holds is still listed, and choosing one moves the whole tab to it.
screener.moneyness_text: A strike within 0.5% of spot at that reading counts as at the money. Above that band a call is out of the money and a put is in it, and below it the other way round.

maxpain.empty_text: No F&O data captured yet — capture starts at the next 15-min reading
maxpain.direction_text: Direction is the latest reading against the reading 4 back (one hour). Flat when the change is under 5% of that series' own largest move away from its first reading today. Fewer than two readings carrying a value is "no baseline" and carries no direction at all. It describes what the number did, never what it does next.
maxpain.gaps_text: A 15-min reading this underlying has no row for keeps its place in the series with no value. The hole is never closed up and no reading is carried forward into it.

direction_detail.rule: Direction is the latest reading against the reading 4 back (one hour). Flat when the change is under 5% of that series' own largest move away from its first reading today. Fewer than two readings carrying a value is "no baseline" and carries no direction at all. It describes what the number did, never what it does next.

maxpain.delta_text: Δ is the change since the previous session's close: this reading's figure minus the same figure at the last 15-min reading of the session before. The same baseline ΔOI uses. A figure with no previous close carries no Δ at all — it is null with a reason, never a zero and never "unchanged".
maxpain.delta_unit_text: Max pain is a STRIKE, so its Δ is in strike points and it moves in whole strike steps — 23,300 to 23,350 is +50 points. A strike change is never shown as a percentage.

maxpain.chain_floors_text: A chain-level figure is withheld when the chain carries fewer than 6 listed call and put contracts, or when one side of it has no open interest at all. This floor is defined by the server, not by the build spec, and the contract count the figure rests on travels with every reading.
maxpain.distance_definition: Distance is the max-pain strike MINUS spot at the same 15-min reading, which is the convention the store itself uses. A positive distance means the strike sits above spot.
maxpain.definition: Max pain is the strike at which the total payout to option buyers at expiry would be smallest, from the open interest standing across every strike of this expiry at that reading. It is read from the metrics worker, not recomputed here, and it moves as open interest moves.

iv.method: bisection on the option price, solved for the volatility
iv.computed_text: Implied volatility is COMPUTED here, not reported by the exchange. It is solved from this option's own last traded price with a Black-Scholes-Merton (European, no dividend) model. Every other number on this tab is a figure the exchange reported.

risk_free_rate_source.text: The risk-free rate is a fixed constant in this server's code — 6.50% a year — not a rate this server fetched from anywhere. No rate feed is connected to it. For a front-month option the solved volatility barely moves with this number; for a far expiry it matters more, and the figure below says by how much.

assumptions.style: European exercise — NSE index and single-stock options are both European-style.
assumptions.dividend: No dividend is subtracted. On a single stock that goes ex-dividend before expiry, this solves slightly high on calls and slightly low on puts.
assumptions.rate: The risk-free rate is a fixed constant in this server's code — 6.50% a year — not a rate this server fetched from anywhere. No rate feed is connected to it. For a front-month option the solved volatility barely moves with this number; for a far expiry it matters more, and the figure below says by how much.
assumptions.day_count: ACT/365, measured from the 15-minute reading to 15:30 IST on the expiry date.
assumptions.price: The option's own last traded price at that reading, as the exchange reported it — never a mid, never a model price.
assumptions.spot: The underlying's spot at the SAME reading. The futures price is not used.
assumptions.american_early_exercise: Not modelled, because these contracts have none.

reason_text.expiry_today: This option expires today, so there is no time left for a volatility to be implied from.
reason_text.no_time_value: The last price is the option's intrinsic value, so no volatility is implied by it.
reason_text.price_below_intrinsic: The last price is below the option's intrinsic value, so the model has no solution.
reason_text.price_above_upper_bound: The last price is at or above the most the option can be worth, so the model has no solution.
reason_text.stale_last_trade: The last trade is older than one 15-minute reading, so this price is not the reading's price.
reason_text.no_convergence: The solver did not settle, so no volatility is reported for this reading.
reason_text.outside_bracket: The price implies a volatility outside 0.01%-1000% a year, which this model does not report.
reason_text.missing_price: No last price was captured for this contract at this reading.
reason_text.missing_spot: No spot price was captured for this underlying at this reading.
reason_text.missing_strike: No strike is stored for this contract.
reason_text.missing_expiry: No expiry date is stored for this contract.
reason_text.non_positive_price: The captured last price is zero or negative, so nothing can be solved from it.
reason_text.unknown_option_type: This contract is not a listed call or put, so no option model applies to it.
reason_text.no_reading: This contract has no row at this 15-min reading.

grid.floors_text: Liquidity floors in force: premium traded ≥ ₹2 cr, OI ≥ 1 lot, last price ≥ ₹1.
grid.empty_text: No F&O data captured yet — capture starts at the next 15-min reading
grid.delta_oi_text: ΔOI is open interest added or removed since the previous close. Every line starts at 0 at the first 15-min reading of the day.
grid.atm_text: ATM is the listed strike nearest spot in the front expiry. ATM+n is n strikes above spot, ATM−n is n strikes below.
grid.direction_text: Direction is the latest ΔOI against the reading 4 back (one hour). Flat when the change is under 5% of that contract's own largest ΔOI today. Fewer than two readings is "no baseline" and carries no direction at all.
grid.not_enough_marks: Not enough readings captured yet — the first line appears after two 15-min readings
grid.price_text: The dashed line on each tile is that contract's own last traded price at the same 15-min readings. It has its own scale — a rupee premium and a count of contracts share no units.
grid.flow_text: Every opened contract has a buyer and a seller. These two lines read which side was paying up at each 15-min reading — they do not say what happens next.
grid.block_text: The line under the block appears only when the calls and the puts are both building over the same window and neither side's total ΔOI change is more than 1.33x the other's. Otherwise nothing is said, because there is nothing to say.
